tools.name: calendars_list
tools.title: List calendars
tools.description: List every calendar of every connected Outlook.com, Microsoft 365 and Google account, each naming its account and provider, its calendarId, whether it is that account's default, whether the account owns it - one merely shared with it is not owned - and its owner's address, its access - edit, read, or freeBusy where Google lets only busy time be read - hidden where the person hid it from their Google list, its own time zone where Google keeps one - Outlook keeps none per calendar - and, under busyShownIn, each other account its busy time shows in. An account that could not be read, or whose events the person does not let you see, is named under unread with why, and one holding more calendars than one answer carries under cutShort.

tools.name: events_list
tools.title: Read events
tools.description: Read the events of a period across every connected calendar, earliest first, or latest first with newestFirst. query finds the events whose title, description, place, organizer or guests hold every word it names - a person by name or address included - on every account: Google searches its own, while Outlook, which searches titles alone, is read across the period and matched here. account, with provider where two share an address, reads that account alone, and calendarId, as calendars_list names it, that one of its calendars alone. Each event answers once, naming under copies every account and calendar holding it, with that copy's id, how it shows there and that account's own answer. An occurrence of a recurring series names under originalStart the start its series gave it, which a moved one keeps, and under each copy that account's seriesId. A calendar shared into one account from another connected account is read through its owner alone. Lumman's own busy copies - private blocks titled "Busy · <the address of the account it copies> (Multi Calendar connector)" - are never among the events: busyCopies answers them apart, one entry per copied busy time with its start and end, the account it copies under copyOf - unknown where no record of it stands - and each account it stands in under standsIn. None counts as the person's time or can be moved or cancelled; asked about one, say it is a busy copy of that account, switched off at https://lumman.co/mcp/account/multi-calendar or by taking that pair away with busy_everywhere_set. Every time is given with its offset in the zone the answer names under timeZone: the one passed, else the person's stored zone, which now names with their time now; an all-day event's start and end are dates, its end the day after its last. An answer, a guest's or an account's own, is accepted, tentative, declined, unanswered or organizer, and one a copy cannot know is left out. An event names its kind where it is no ordinary event - a Google outOfOffice, focusTime, workingLocation, birthday or fromGmail entry - its privacy where it is not normal: public, private, confidential or personal - and its Teams, Zoom or Meet join link, and each copy its webLink; an out-of-office event shows as away. A description is its first 255 characters, marked descriptionCut where it goes on: events_get reads it whole. Each calendar answers at most 50 events, read in time order; one with more is named under cutShort with its calendarId, readTo - the start of the last event read - and continueAt: pass that continueAt with its account and calendarId, the same period and query, to read on from exactly where it stopped; read latest first, such a calendar's latest events are the ones past readTo, so read it on before naming the latest. A calendar or an account that could not be read, or that the person does not let you see, is named under unread with why: needs_reconnection - reconnected at https://lumman.co/mcp/account/multi-calendar - not_allowed, refused, gone, rate_limited or unavailable; where nothing could be read the answer is an error. malformed counts events a provider sent in a form that could not be read, each left out. An event whose words screen as a prompt attack is left out and named under withheld by its start, its end and each copy's account, calendarId and id - by account alone where an id screened so - and a calendar whose name screened so is named by its account alone.

to.description: End of the period, excluded, in the same forms.

timeZone.description: An IANA zone such as Europe/London to answer in; the person's stored one where omitted.

query.description: Words, or a person by name or address, every one of which an event must hold.

account.description: Read this connected account alone, by the address calendars_list names.

provider.description: The account's provider, as calendars_list names it; needed only where two connected accounts share an address.

calendarId.description: Read this calendar of the account named alone, by the calendarId calendars_list names.

continueAt.description: Read on from where a calendar under cutShort was cut: its continueAt, with its account and calendarId.

tools.name: free_times_find
tools.title: Find a time
tools.description: Find when the person is free in every connected calendar: each stretch of a window that no busy time touches and that is at least as long as the meeting. An event holds its time as its provider's own free/busy shows it: on Google unless shown as available or declined - an invitation not yet answered or answered maybe included - and on Outlook only when shown busy or away, so an Outlook tentative answer leaves its time free; a cancelled event holds none. An all-day event holding time holds its whole day in the person's own time zone. The search never starts before now, keeps to every preference preferences_get names and to the window's first 365 days and, where the call names them, to hours on each day and to weekdays on top of those preferences; limit keeps the earliest stretches. Once any day has working hours, a day without them is off. The buffers pad the meeting being booked: a stretch starts buffer_before_minutes after busy time ends and ends buffer_after_minutes before the next begins. Each stretch answers once, in time order, with its parts inside the preferred times under preferred. Times, hours and weekdays are in the zone the call names, else the person's own; the stored working hours and preferred times are in the person's own. searched names the window searched and narrowedBy what narrowed it: notice, the least notice from now, rounded up to the quarter hour; horizon, to the end of its last day; yearCap, the 365 days; readLimit, a calendar holding more events than a search reads, read as far as it could be and searched to two days before the last it read; daysOff, days without working hours; fullDays, days already holding the most meetings in a day, a meeting being an event of some length that holds time inside that day's working hours. A calendar or account named under unread was not counted, nor were the calendars past the first 100 of an account under cutShort, so their busy time may fall inside a stretch; an account needing reconnection is reconnected at https://lumman.co/mcp/account/multi-calendar.

from.description: Start of the window, included, with its offset, e.g. 2026-10-12T09:00:00+01:00.

to.description: End of the window, excluded, with its offset.

minutes.description: Meeting length in minutes; the stored one where omitted.

timeZone.description: An IANA zone such as Europe/London the answer is given in; the stored one where omitted.

hours.description: Only these hours of each day, e.g. 10:00-16:00 or 09:00-12:00, 14:00-17:00.

weekdays.description: Only these days of the week.

limit.description: At most this many stretches, the earliest.

tools.name: events_create
tools.title: Create an event
tools.description: Create an event in one of a connected account's own calendars: the one named by the calendarId calendars_list gives, else the account's default; a calendar only shared with the account is refused. Guests are invited by that account's provider, Microsoft or Google, from its own address. A timed event's start and end are instants with their offset, the end no earlier than the start, so an entry of no length is taken; an all-day event's are dates, its end the day after its last. It is written in the person's own time zone, so an invitation shows that zone's time, and the answer gives its times in the zone it names under timeZone. A meeting with guests, no location and no video gets the person's default meeting link as its place. How it shows, its privacy, reminders, kind and video link are each refused with the reason where the account's provider lacks them. An Outlook subject takes at most 255 characters. repeat makes it a recurring series, each occurrence keeping the start's own hour in the person's time zone across clock changes. Who hears of it is notify's choice. Repeating a create whose answer was lost, with the same arguments, finds the event the first made rather than making a second - for the rest of that day (UTC), on Outlook only while Microsoft also recognises the repeat - so two events meant as two differ in some argument. Each guest's own times are answered under guestTimes in their time zone where it is known - the one guestZones names for them, else the one a member of the person's circles stored - and any other guest's zone as unknown, their time counted as the person's. A meeting any part of which falls, for a guest of known zone, outside 09:00-18:00 or on a Saturday or Sunday in that zone - an all-day one only on a Saturday or Sunday - is not sent: the refusal names each such guest and their time, and it goes out only once the call passes unusualHoursAgreed true on the person's word. A series is checked by its first occurrence; the person's own hours are never held.

account.description: The connected account, by the address calendars_list names.

provider.description: The account's provider, as calendars_list names it; needed only where two connected accounts share an address.

calendarId.description: The calendar to create it in, by the calendarId calendars_list names; the account's default where omitted.

guestZones.description: A guest's own time zone, only as the person names it - never inferred from an address, a language or a provider.

unusualHoursAgreed.description: True only once the person has agreed to send at the hours an answer named as unusual for a guest.

showAs.description: How it shows; Google shows busy or free alone. Busy where omitted.

reminders.description: Minutes before its start each reminder sounds, Outlook keeping one; empty for none, the calendar's own where omitted.

kind.description: Google makes either only in a Workspace account's main calendar, timed; Outlook makes out of office alone, shown away.

video.description: A Meet link on a Google account or a Teams link on a work Microsoft account, given back under joinUrl.

notify.description: Who the provider tells: every guest where omitted, externalOnly only guests outside Google Calendar, none nobody. Outlook tells every guest of a meeting it makes, changes or cancels, so there only an answer goes untold.

repeat.description: Makes it a recurring series, from its start, without end unless until or count is named.

every.description: A month repeats on the start's day of the month, a year on its date.

interval.description: Every how many days, weeks, months or years; 1 where omitted.

days.description: The days a weekly series falls on; the start's own where omitted.

until.description: The last date an occurrence may fall on.

tools.name: events_edit
tools.title: Change an event
tools.description: Change an event the account organises, in place and in one call: its subject, body, location, start and end, how it shows, its privacy, reminders and video link, and its guests - addGuests invited, removeGuests taken off. Only what is named changes: the event keeps its id, every other guest's answer and its join link, a start named alone keeps its length and an end named alone keeps its start. Start and end are named as events_create names them, so naming both in the other form turns a timed event all-day or back, and are written in the person's own time zone as events_create writes them. What the account's provider lacks is refused with the reason, as on events_create, and so is a new body for an Outlook online meeting, whose join details it holds. Changing guests takes inviting allowed on the account. A whole series' start and end are its first occurrence's, and a change to a whole series holding occurrences changed apart from it is refused, naming each by when its series set it, so none of theirs is undone. Its provider sends a meeting's guests the change from the account's own address, as notify chooses. Like every write, the answer names the event's provider, its calendarId where its provider addresses it by one, and its webLink. Guests' own hours hold a change as they hold events_create: every guest's where its times change, an added guest's at its time otherwise.

account.description: The connected account, by the address calendars_list names.

provider.description: The account's provider, as calendars_list names it; needed only where two connected accounts share an address.

calendarId.description: The calendar holding the event, by the calendarId events_list names; a Google account's event outside its default calendar needs it.

eventId.description: The event's id, as events_list names it.

scope.description: For an occurrence of a recurring series: occurrence, where omitted, acts on that occurrence alone, series on its whole series. A series named by its own seriesId is refused unless series is passed.

showAs.description: How it shows; Google shows busy or free alone.

reminders.description: Minutes before its start each reminder sounds, Outlook keeping one; empty for none.

video.description: A Meet link on a Google account or a Teams link on a work Microsoft account, given back under joinUrl.

removeGuests.description: Guests to take off, by address.

notify.description: Who the provider tells: every guest where omitted, externalOnly only guests outside Google Calendar, none nobody. Outlook tells every guest of a meeting it makes, changes or cancels, so there only an answer goes untold.

guestZones.description: A guest's own time zone, only as the person names it - never inferred from an address, a language or a provider.

unusualHoursAgreed.description: True only once the person has agreed to send at the hours an answer named as unusual for a guest.

tools.name: preferences_get
tools.title: Read scheduling preferences
tools.description: Read the person's scheduling preferences, as preferences_set describes each, null where unset; once any day's hours are set, a day without is off; receiving names the calendar bookings are made in. calendars_list says which calendars count as busy.
